gap: No result ChatGPT got states a figure measured by a named reviewer or lab (tested load, loaded spin, wobble or measured usable diameter) for any cabinet turntable, and in about 20 tool calls I found no such figure to add.
standout_why: I read four result pages ChatGPT got. bazpedia.com ('8 Best Lazy Susan Cabinet Organizers… Tested', dated 2026-09-16) has only test claims from its own unnamed author or team, such as 'spun under six cans of tomatoes'. Its OXO 16-in '20+ lbs without wobble' has no source. kitchendesignnotes.com (2026-11-07) says its figures come from Amazon listings and maker specs, such as Dowell 40 lb per shelf and Rev-A-Shelf 20 to 64 lb per shelf, and that the author has not used the products. 4stnotary.com says 'we have not tested these lazy Susans ourselves' and uses only maker and Amazon data. Outside those results, Food & Wine and Reviewed give specs with no measured figures, and Family Handyman gives no measured figures at all. Consumer Reports covered a different product, a dining-table turntable, and its open text has no figures. The outlets most likely to have measured figures (Serious Eats, The Spruce, Good Housekeeping, NYT Wirecutter, America's Test Kitchen) block this tool, and Apartment Therapy and The Kitchn returned 403. So none of their numbers could be opened. Every load figure on the rival pages and the open outlet pages is a maker rating or comes from an unnamed person. Because this angle adds nothing a rival lacks, I scored it 0 even though no rival has the measurement either.
decides: It doesn't change or confirm a pick. I found no named measurement to rank the OXO 11-in tray, the Dowell kidney corner unit or the Everbilt 6-in bearing. The pick for 'turntable for cabinet' has to rest on fit (cabinet opening and interior diameter, from the makers' spec sheets), the type the shopper needs (tray, built-in corner unit or bare bearing) and maker load ratings. Those are angles other than E. This category (non-electronic kitchen storage) also falls outside Dealectric's product list, which has no lazy susan or cabinet-hardware listings.

unsourced: A named lab's or reviewer's tested load, loaded-spin or wobble figure for the OXO Good Grips 11-in turntable. Search found no Serious Eats, Wirecutter, ATK or Good Housekeeping test. Seriouseats.com and thespruce.com refused the fetch tool, and the search tool won't search them, Good Housekeeping, NYT or ATK at all.
Apartment Therapy's own measurement of the OXO 16-in 'Not So Lazy Susan' usable diameter (the search snippet said about 14 in): the page returned 403, so I didn't use the figure.
The Kitchn's 'The 11 Best Lazy Susans, According to Pro Organizers': the page returned 403.
Any independent measurement of the Dowell 2-shelf kidney unit (rotation, sag under load, real interior clearance): I found no reviewer or lab that measured it.
Any independent load or wobble test of 6-in square lazy-susan bearings (Everbilt, Shepherd): I found only maker ratings and a Sawmill Creek forum suggestion, no measured comparison.
Prices: I didn't check them today because this angle is measurements only. The OXO $15.71, Dowell $109.99 and Everbilt $7.87 figures are ChatGPT's card prices, not checked.
